title: Common-stage additive and shift calculus
statement:
The equivalence relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is
reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Transport is additive and obeys
$(u_N)_P=u_P$ for $M\subset N\subset P$. The common-stage operations are
representative-independent and make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category.
Every finite diagram of objects, morphisms, composites, and asserted
equalities in $\mathcal P_T$ is represented over one finite field, and an
asserted equality holds exactly when it holds after passage to a further
common stage.

Define
$$
 (E,K)[1]=(E,K[1])
$$
and, for $f=[M,u]:(E,K)\to(F,L)$, define
$$
 f[1]=\left[M,
 \sigma_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ u[1]\circ\sigma_{M/E,K}\right].
$$
This gives a well-defined additive autoequivalence $[1]$ with inverse
$[-1]$, and every finite-stage inclusion
$j_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal P_T$ commutes with shifts through the
specified comparison.

asserted equalities must first be transported to one common stage.

proof.text: Reuse the existing exactUnitLocus and uniformProfileLocus theorems from [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated] through a private import-all. The integral subcategory is the intersection of two triangulated object properties. The exact completion data in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-completion-data] identifies completeness with invertibility of the completion unit. Naturality and its shift compatibility show this property is closed under isomorphisms, shifts, zero objects and distinguished triangles. By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-reduction-criterion], the uniform reduction condition is equivalent to a bounded cohomology interval together with constructibility of every reduced cohomology sheaf. Shift the interval by the negative of the shift degree; triangle closure follows from the bounded standard t-structure and [lem-weil-constructible-coefficient-homology-triangulated]. Thus the integral property is triangulated, without needing a dimension bound or invertibility of the prime for this closure argument. Its full inclusion gives additive, integral-ring-linear shifts.

Extend each integral shift to raw tensor Hom modules by ScalarLocalization.map. Map the integral shift-zero and shift-add isomorphisms through localization. Their naturality is verified on pure tensors and extended by additivity. Applying localization to the integral shift coherence identities gives ShiftMkCore and hence HasShift. Equality of its functors and of every zero and addition component determines the entire monoidal shift structure, so the prescribed normalization has a unique solution.

The localization shift comparison has identity components. Naturality follows from the tensor Hom formula, and its unit and addition coherence are the localized integral identities. The component normalization determines this CommShift structure uniquely. For scalar extension use the canonical shift on derived restriction, its adjunction mate on ambient tensor extension, and reflection through the fully faithful integral inclusion. Reuse pbcScalarLocalization_isLocalization from [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension] to identify the raw tensor-Hom rationalization as a localization. Reuse its pbcKanCommShift_ext to compare shift structures degreewise. The integral/rational comparison then uniquely descends the scalar CommShift structure by the localization lifting API and natural-transformation extensionality.

The ambient scalar associator is the adjunction mate of derived restriction composition. The derived exact-functor composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons commute with shifts. Units, counits, whiskering, associators and unitors commute with shifts, so the mate does as well. Express the integral associator after its faithful inclusion by this ambient equation and the identity comparison squares; reflect shift compatibility. Express the rational associator after integral localization by its normalized component equation, a composition of the two scalar comparison squares, the localized integral associator and the inverse composite comparison. Every factor commutes with shifts; reflect along the object-surjective localization.

A triangulated integral full subcategory has finite biproducts. Its raw rationalization is additive and surjective on objects, so the additive essential-surjectivity theorem transports finite products to it. In a preadditive category these finite products give finite biproducts, including the empty biproduct and hence a zero object.

Use the actual StageSystem of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Its associator and unit identities give the transport cocycle, and additivity gives transport of sums and negatives. The representative equivalence relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive by transporting finitely many equality witnesses to a common upper stage. The preadditive quotient construction already supplies representative-independent addition and composition and all their category laws.

For any finite family of pair objects choose one upper stage for their coefficient stages using directedness. Replace each pair object by its canonical isomorphic toStage object. The inclusion from this common stage is additive (by the representative addition formula), hence preserves its finite products. Transport this product along the object isomorphisms to obtain a product of the original pair objects. Their preadditive structure turns it into the required biproduct. This also treats the empty family.

For a finite graph choose one stage containing the stages of its objects and representatives of all its arrows. The toStage isomorphisms identify its arrows with the corresponding included common-stage maps. Each equality in a finite list has a further-stage witness by the quotient relation; directedness gives a common upper bound for all the witnesses. Conversely, a simultaneous common-stage equality gives each quotient equality. Empty lists need no additional witnesses.

The stage scalar comparisons and associator shift compatibility prove the representative shift formula respects transport. Naturality, cancellation of inverse shift comparisons and additivity show that it preserves identities, composition and sums. Descend this representative formula to the quotient for every integer shift.

Take the integral-stage shift-zero and shift-add components as quotient representatives, conjugating by scalar shift comparisons as required by the representative formula. Their naturality and coherence follow after transport to one stage from the finite-stage shift laws. ShiftMkCore supplies the coherent integer shift, hence the inverse shifts. The stage inclusion comparisons have identity representatives and satisfy the same unit and addition laws. Combine these facts with the finite-diagram, equality-detection and biproduct results to obtain commonStageCalculus.

proof.text:
The relation of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] is reflexive and
symmetric from the definitions, and transitive: if $(M,u)\sim(N,v)$ and
$(N,v)\sim(Q,w)$ with witnesses $P_1,P_2$, transport all to their compositum
$P$, where both equalities hold by the transport formula $(u_N)_P=u_P$ and
the unit/associator equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. The same
formula shows that transport is additive and satisfies $(u_N)_P=u_P$ for
$M\subset N\subset P$ (the associator cocycle), so addition, negatives,
identities and composition, computed after transport to one common finite
field, are independent of the representatives and of the field; the
finite-stage additive category laws transported to a common field (with
$T_{F/E}$ additive) make $\mathcal P_T$ an additive category. Every finite
diagram is represented over one finite field by transporting objects and
morphisms (via the $\gamma$-isomorphisms of
[def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]), and a finite list of asserted
equalities holds in $\mathcal P_T$ exactly when the transported equalities
hold over a further common stage, by the definition of the equivalence. For
the shift: equivalent representatives define equivalent shifted
representatives by naturality of $\sigma$ and the associator equations of
[prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], so $[1]$ and $[-1]$ are well-defined
additive endofunctors, $[1]$ has inverse $[-1]$ (the finite-stage shift
laws), and the inclusion $j_E$ commutes with the shifts through the
specified comparison.
